concepts.label: vertex
concepts.gloss: A vertex is a forwarding realm within a fabric at which links terminate and access, adaptation, switching, or circuit-endpoint functions may reside.
concepts.example: R1 is a vertex in the zeta-over-optical realm: span-R1-R2 terminates there, and the crr4/grd2 bridging adaptation is performed there.
concepts.evidence: Read as a network node from kind `node`, membership in fabric a09, and router/access-node instances R1–R3 and A1–A3; ruled out span a08, which connects vertices rather than acting as one.

concepts.label: span-cap-point
concepts.gloss: A span-cap-point is the vertex-owned termination point at which one end of a network span is attached to a vertex.
concepts.example: hep-R1-R2 is the termination on R1 for span-R1-R2, anchoring that span at the R1 vertex.
concepts.evidence: Read as a link-facing termination from kind `termination`, relations `on-vertex` a01 and `terminates` a08, and hep-R1-R2-style instances; ruled out access point a04 and service endpoint a10, which face services rather than terminate spans.

concepts.label: shifting-span
concepts.gloss: A shifting-span is a vertex-local adaptation that bridges a carried stream between the tiers or multiplex contexts identified by a tier-stream qualifier.
concepts.example: At R1, the `crr4/grd2 bridging` shifting-span adapts the grd2 stream into the crr4 context specified by `grd2 mapped into crr4`.
concepts.evidence: Read as an inter-tier adaptation from kind `adaptation`, its location at vertex a01, its `adapts` relation to qualifier a06, and instance `crr4/grd2 bridging at R1`; ruled out gate set a07, which switches traffic without expressing a tier mapping.

concepts.label: offer-gateway-point
concepts.gloss: An offer-gateway-point is an access-facing point on a vertex through which a customer or edge attachment enters or leaves a carriage offer.
concepts.example: acp-A1-grd on vertex A1 is the ingress access point for the grd carriage offer from A1 toward A3, while acp-A3-grd provides the corresponding egress access.
concepts.evidence: Read as a service-access attachment from kind `access`, relations `on-vertex` a01 and `accesses` carriage-offer a05, and acp-A1-grd/acp-A3-grd instances; ruled out a02 link terminations and a10 circuit endpoints.

concepts.label: carriage-offer
concepts.gloss: A carriage-offer is an end-to-end transport service over a fabric that carries a specified tier stream between access gateway points and is realized by associated circuit endpoints.
concepts.example: co-a1a3-grd2 carries the grd2 stream from acp-A1-grd to acp-A3-grd over the zeta-over-optical realm and is represented internally by cxp-a1a3-R1 and cxp-a1a3-R3.
concepts.evidence: Read as an end-to-end transport service from kind `service`, its use of access points a04, realization by circuit endpoints a10, operation over fabric a09, and instance `co-a1a3-grd2 (grd2, A1 to A3)`; ruled out physical span a08.

concepts.label: tier-stream-qualifier
concepts.gloss: A tier-stream-qualifier specifies the multiplex stream and tier mapping under which a carriage offer is carried or interpreted.
concepts.example: For co-a1a3-grd2, the qualifier `grd2 mapped into crr4` states that the offered grd2 stream occupies or is conveyed within the crr4 multiplex tier.
concepts.evidence: Read as a multiplex-layer qualification from kind `multiplex`, relation `qualifies` carriage-offer a05, and instance `grd2 mapped into crr4`; ruled out shifting-span a03, which performs the adaptation rather than describing its stream/tier mapping.

concepts.label: vertex-gate-set
concepts.gloss: A vertex-gate-set is the collection of switching gates at a vertex through which compatible terminations or flows can be cross-connected.
concepts.example: The R2 cross-switch gate set can select a cross-connection through R2 between traffic arriving from span-R1-R2 and traffic leaving on span-R2-R3.
concepts.evidence: Read as a node-local switching construct from kind `switching`, relation `on-vertex` a01, and instance `R2 cross-switch gate set`; ruled out adaptation a03, which maps between tiers rather than selecting cross-connections.

concepts.label: span
concepts.gloss: A span is a network link between vertices whose ends are anchored by span-cap-points on those vertices.
concepts.example: span-R1-R2 connects vertices R1 and R2, with hep-R1-R2 providing its R1-side termination and a corresponding span-cap-point providing its R2-side termination.
concepts.evidence: Read as a point-to-point network link from kind `link`, relation `between` vertices a01, reciprocal termination by a02, and span-R1-R2/span-A1-R1 instances; ruled out carriage-offer a05, which is an end-to-end service over the topology.

concepts.label: fabric
concepts.gloss: A fabric is a multi-tier network topology that contains the forwarding vertices and spans over which carriage offers are delivered.
concepts.example: The zeta-over-optical realm is a fabric containing vertices such as R1, R2, R3, A1, A2, and A3 and spans such as span-R1-R2 and span-A1-R1.
concepts.evidence: Read as the enclosing network topology from kind `topology`, containment of vertices a01 and spans a08, and instance `the zeta-over-optical realm`; ruled out vertex a01, which is an element inside the fabric.

concepts.label: circuit-end-point
concepts.gloss: A circuit-end-point is a vertex-local endpoint of the internal circuit that realizes a carriage offer within the fabric.
concepts.example: cxp-a1a3-R1 and cxp-a1a3-R3 are the two circuit endpoints on R1 and R3 that realize the internal path for co-a1a3-grd2.
concepts.evidence: Read as an endpoint of a service-realizing circuit from kind `endpoint`, relations `on-vertex` a01 and `part-of` carriage-offer a05, and paired cxp-a1a3-R1/R3 instances; ruled out offer-gateway-point a04, which is the external access point, and span-cap-point a02, which terminates a link.
